implementation.mapping: Group G output row tiles, then walk rows first inside each output column of the group; use actual row count for the last group.
implementation.native_dw_axes: Output rows are N features, columns are K features; reduction is M batch.
implementation.persistent_assignment: task = blockIdx.x + iteration * gridDim.x; grouping changes only task-to-coordinate mapping.
implementation.baseline: Saved pre-change binary; also compare new binary group1 to reveal mapping-branch/code-generation overhead.

sweep.method: Warm CUDA graphs; all variants share input/output buffers; rotated timing order; unlocked clocks; paired ratios by round.

square_confirmation.method: Warm CUDA graphs; all variants share input/output buffers; rotated timing order; unlocked clocks; paired ratios by round.

full_backward.method: Warm CUDA graphs; all variants share input/output buffers; rotated timing order; unlocked clocks; paired ratios by round.

sanitizers.racecheck: RACECHECK SUMMARY: 0 hazards displayed (0 errors, 0 warnings)

validation.numerics: Exact independent dyadic FP64 oracle, all 8 native-dW configs and swap modes; short groups, TMA tails, data refresh, streams, CUDA graphs; benchmark variants bitwise equal.

conclusions: Initial candidates: 1,8,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,18,20. Initial sweep shows a repeatable small standalone dW win only at M=N=K=4096.

Higher-repeat square sweep additionally tested 24,26,32. Groups16-26 form a plateau around 1.021-1.023x versus the old binary; group13 is 1.019x. Do not over-interpret the tiny difference between group18 and group26.
The warmed standalone dW benefit does not transfer in full to full backward: square paired speedup is only about 1.003x with group26. Larger input shape slows by roughly 0.6-1.0% in full backward.
Keep row-major group1 as default. Grouped rasterization is exposed as an experimental plan option rather than imposing a shape-specific regression on other workloads.
Measurements use unlocked clocks and sustained warm-up with rotated graph timing. Compare variants within a run; do not compare absolute times directly with previous colder/unprofiled measurements.
Cache-locality explanations are hypotheses here; this task did not collect new NCU profiles of grouped variants. Reordering does not change the number of tiles assigned to each persistent CTA.
